title: Digital Systems 1
objectives:
This course covers the design and analysis of digital logic circuits including combinatorial
and sequential logic circuits.
syllabus:
Number systems, binary systems, binary codes, addition, substraction, multiplication and
division, Boolean algebra, theorems, logic functions, sum-of-products form, product-of-sums
form, Karnaugh maps, logic minimization using K-maps, logic gates (RTL, DTL, TTL) and
related topics (FAN-IN, FAN-OUT), combinatorial circuits design, multiplexers, decoders,
comparators, sequential circuits design, flip-flops, shift registers, counters, synchronous and
asynchronous logic circuits, finite state machines, timing of sequential circuits, Hamming and
ASCII codes, TTL and MOS technologies.
Evaluation:
textbooks:
1. Morris Mano, Michael Ciletti, Digital Design. 4th ed. Prentice Hall, 2006.
2. Victor Nelson, Troy Nagle, Bill Carroll, David Irwin, Digital Logic Circuit Analysis and
Design. 1st ed. Prentice Hall, 1995.
3. A. P. Godse, Digital Logic Circuits. 2nd ed. Technical Publications, 2011.
